name: tumble-in
phrase: tumble in with a rotating flip
concept: The element cartwheels in from the side with a full rotation, then lands upright. Use it for a lively, physical entrance, like a toy rolling onto the screen.

name: cartwheel-in
concept: The element arcs in from a corner while it spins a full turn, like a cartwheel. It gives a big, showy arrival for hero elements or celebratory moments.

name: barrel-roll-in
phrase: barrel roll in with a scale pulse
concept: The element grows and spins a full 360 degrees at once, like an airplane barrel roll. It suits confident, game-like entrances for icons and badges.

name: flip-tumble-in
phrase: flip in thin then snap flat
concept: The element flattens to a sliver, rotates, then springs back to full shape. It reads like a card flipping into place with extra snap.

name: roll-in-bounce
concept: The element rolls in from the left with a spin, then gives one small bounce before it settles. Use it for a playful item that rolls to a stop.

name: corkscrew-in
concept: The element spirals in from a corner with multiple rotations while it shrinks into place. It feels tight and energetic, like a screw driving in.

name: somersault-in
concept: The element drops in from above while it flips a full rotation, then lands flat. Use it for a lively drop entrance, like a gymnast landing.

name: hop-in
phrase: hop in with three small bounces
concept: The element drops in and hops three times, with each hop smaller than the last, then rests. It suits a cheerful, bouncy arrival for small UI items.

name: bunny-hop-in
phrase: bunny hop in with two big squashes
concept: The element drops with two big hops, each landing with a squash before it springs up again. It gives a bouncy, cartoon-like arrival.

name: skip-in
concept: The element skips in sideways with small diagonal hops that shrink as it goes, like a child skipping into a room. It feels light and cheerful.

name: bounce-hop-in
phrase: bounce in like a thrown ball
concept: The element arcs in diagonally, then bounces vertically a few times as it settles, like a ball tossed onto the screen. Use it for a fun, physical arrival.

name: pogo-in
phrase: pogo in with one strong squash
concept: The element compresses, springs up high, then squashes again before it settles, like one strong pogo-stick jump. It gives a single, punchy bouncy entrance.

name: hiccup-in
concept: The element flickers and jitters upward in small uneven steps before it settles, like a hiccup. Use it for a quirky, comic entrance.

name: overshoot-settle-in
phrase: pop in and wobble to rest
concept: The element scales past full size, then rocks side to side before it settles still. Use it for a friendly pop that has extra personality.

name: rubber-band-in
concept: The element stretches wide, then tall, then narrows back to shape, like a rubber band snapping into place. It gives a stretchy, elastic entrance.

name: teeter-in
concept: The element pops to full size, then teeters left and right with shrinking swings before it holds still. Use it for a charming, off-balance arrival.

name: tilt-in-settle
concept: The element slides in at a tilt, then straightens as it reaches its resting spot. It suits a quick, confident arrival with a bit of flair.

name: jelly-in
phrase: jelly in with a soft jiggle
concept: The element grows in with a soft, repeating jiggle that fades out, like a gelatin wobble. Use it for a squishy, friendly entrance.

name: wag-in
concept: The element pops in, then wags side to side like a tail, with each swing smaller than the last. It gives a friendly, eager arrival.

name: skid-in
phrase: skid in to a sharp stop
concept: The element slides in fast, overshoots slightly, then corrects to a sharp stop, like a skid on a floor. Use it for a fast, confident arrival.

name: skid-stop-in
concept: The element slides in fast while it tilts and stretches slightly, then straightens as it stops, like a car skidding to a halt. It suits an energetic, physical arrival.

name: brake-in
phrase: brake in with a hard stop
concept: The element falls fast, stretches slightly in the fall, then squashes and rebounds a touch as it brakes to a stop. Use it for a sudden, forceful arrival.

name: drift-in
concept: The element slides in diagonally while it rotates like a drifting car, then straightens as it settles into place. It gives a stylish, energetic arrival.
keywords: slide and drift to a stop

name: screech-in
concept: The element streaks in fast with a motion blur that clears as it snaps to a stop. Use it for a high-speed, dramatic entrance.

name: spring-in-diagonal
concept: The element springs in from a corner, grows past full size, then settles evenly on both axes. Use it for a bouncy, symmetric diagonal arrival.

name: zigzag-in
concept: The element slides in while it changes direction twice, like a zigzag path, before it settles. It gives a snappy, energetic sideways arrival.

name: boing-in
concept: The element squashes wide then stretches tall in alternating beats, like a classic cartoon boing. Use it for the most rubbery, bouncy entrance in the set.

name: jack-in-the-box
concept: The element springs open from nothing with a rotating pop, then rocks briefly before it settles. Use it for a surprise, playful reveal.

name: trampoline-in
concept: The element drops from high up and bounces on an invisible trampoline, with each bounce lower and flatter, until it rests. Use it for a long, joyful bouncy entrance.

name: spiral-pop-in
concept: The element spins several full turns while it grows from tiny to full size, then settles still. Use it for a fast, dizzying pop entrance.

name: slam-in
concept: The element drops in fast and oversized, slams down to size, then recoils slightly before it settles. Use it for a bold, forceful arrival.

name: power-slam-in
concept: The element shrinks fast from a huge size, slams into place, then recoils with a tiny rotation before it settles. It gives a dramatic, high-impact arrival.

name: stomp-in
concept: The element drops in and squashes flat on landing, then rebounds slightly before it settles, like a heavy stomp. Use it for a weighty, powerful arrival.

name: crash-land-in
phrase: crash land in at an angle
concept: The element flies in diagonally and oversized, crashes into place with a tilt, then wobbles briefly before it settles. Use it for a chaotic, energetic arrival.

name: ricochet-in
concept: The element bounces off an invisible wall to the right, then back left, with each bounce smaller until it settles. Use it for a snappy, pinball-like arrival.

name: yo-yo-in
concept: The element drops, rises back up, then dips again in a shrinking rhythm, like a yo-yo settling on its string. Use it for a playful up-down arrival.

name: accordion-in
concept: The element squeezes flat, then expands and contracts vertically a few times, like an accordion, before it settles. Use it for a springy vertical entrance.

name: wiggle-walk-in
concept: The element slides in while it rocks left and right in a steady rhythm, like a playful walk, then straightens as it settles. Use it for a cheerful, animated arrival.

name: star-burst-in
phrase: star-burst in with a quick pop
concept: The element bursts in from tiny with a fast overshoot and a small spin, then settles almost instantly. Use it for a sharp, exciting quick reveal.

name: flicker-hop-in
concept: The element flickers in visibility as it rises, then gives one clean hop before it settles. Use it for a glitchy, energetic reveal with a bouncy finish.

name: torque-in
concept: The element spins in from a wide angle, then oscillates back and forth with shrinking swings until it points straight. Use it for a torsion-spring style entrance.

name: pinball-in
concept: The element bounces in from a corner along a zigzag diagonal path, with a small rotate at each bounce, like a pinball in play. Use it for a chaotic, arcade-style arrival.

name: elastic-drop-in
concept: The element falls while it stretches, squashes on landing, then rebounds a few times with shrinking elasticity. Use it for a rubbery, physics-driven drop entrance.

name: cannon-in
concept: The element launches in from far off screen at high speed, then eases to a near-instant stop. Use it for a bold, whoosh-style fast entrance.

name: bobblehead-in
concept: The element pops to size, then nods back and forth in small, quick swings that fade out, like a bobblehead toy. Use it for a cute, twitchy settle.

name: kangaroo-in
phrase: kangaroo in with a big leap
concept: The element leaps in with a single high, tilted arc, then lands and straightens as it settles. Use it for a bold, single-bound entrance.

name: dizzy-in
phrase: dizzy in with a double spin
concept: The element grows in while it spins two full turns, then wobbles briefly before it stops still. Use it for a whirling, slightly disoriented arrival.

name: pounce-in
concept: The element crouches low and wide, then leaps forward to land and settle at full size. Use it for a predatory, playful pounce entrance.

name: firecracker-in
concept: The element snaps rapidly in several small directions before it settles still, like a firecracker's crackle. Use it for a hyper, fizzy burst of energy.

name: gummy-drop-in
concept: The element drops and squashes very flat, then stretches and settles through a few soft, gooey bounces. Use it for a squishy, candy-like landing.
